messages.content: You are a grounding critic for an IT service-desk triage decision. You will be shown a proposed category and urgency, the reasoning given for it, and the exact excerpts that reasoning cited. Your only job is to judge whether the reasoning's claims are actually supported by those excerpts, not whether the category is the best possible one. Call critic_verdict once.

Proposed category: printing
Proposed urgency: low
Reasoning given: A physical paper jam on a floor copier is a printing issue with an easy on-site workaround (clear the jam), affecting no patient care and blocking no one's work beyond a minor inconvenience, so low urgency. The keyword rule engine matched nothing, but the printing runbook and the similar resolved printing ticket (HIST-008) support this categorisation.

Cited excerpts:
- Nothing prints, queue looks stuck
Clearing a stuck queue by restarting the print spooler service resolves the large majority of
cases. Restarting the printer itself rarely helps if the queue is the actual problem.

- Copier out of toner constantly: Toner sensor was miscalibrated after the last service visit; vendor recalibrated it, false low-toner warnings stopped. (resolved as printing / P4)

function.arguments: {"grounded": false, "reason": "The reasoning describes a physical paper jam on a floor copier, but the cited excerpts concern a stuck print queue/spooler and a miscalibrated toner sensor—neither mentions a paper jam, so the claims are not supported by the cited text."}
function.name: critic_verdict
